Resource: FHIR Version: R4B (4.3.0) — base resource: MedicationAdministration, unchanged in structure between R4 and R4B. Used instead of MedicationRequest because emergency care is administration-heavy — drugs are given in real time, not merely prescribed.

Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Canonical FHIR ValueSet (required binding): in-progress | not-done | on-hold | completed | entered-in-error | stopped | unknown. 'not-done' matters — capture an attempted-but-withheld administration (e.g. allergy caught just in time), not just successful ones.

REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Use medicationCodeableConcept rather than medicationReference(Medication) unless you already maintain a Medication resource catalog — simpler for a field EMT app.

Description: The patient who received the medication.
The encounter the administration occurred in — typically EMPOCEncounter.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) — tightened from the base spec's optional 0..1 binding for this profile, since every emergency drug administration must be traceable to a specific encounter for both clinical and SHA claims purposes.

Description: Exact time the drug was given (or start/end for an infusion).
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT — this is the core real-time administration record; exact timing matters for drug-interaction windows and protocol timing (e.g. epinephrine redosing intervals in resuscitation).
MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..*) — recommended to always populate in practice.

Description: The specific EMT/paramedic/clinician who gave the drug.
Dose, route, and rate of administration.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — strongly recommended to populate given the clinical/legal weight of dosing accuracy, but not forced to 1..1 to avoid rejecting a record if a field app fails to capture structured dosage in a chaotic scene.

Description: The amount given, e.g. 1 mg, 0.3 mg.
Route of administration, e.g. IV, IM, IO, inhaled.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — route materially changes onset/effect and is frequently reviewed in case audits; populate whenever the dosage element itself is used.

Description: Infusion rate, if the drug was given as a continuous infusion rather than a bolus.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support. Only relevant for infusions, uncommon relative to bolus dosing in field EMS care.

Description: Why the medication was given, e.g. linked to the working diagnosis/symptom.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support. Nice to have for audit/reporting but the clinical reasoning is usually already evident from the linked Condition/Encounter.

Description: Number of attempts made to administer this medication. Maps to medications[].attempts.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — newly identified from real handover data. Relevant for repeated-dose protocols and difficult-access scenarios (e.g. multiple IV attempts before a drug was successfully given); do not conflate with dosage — this counts administration attempts, not the number of doses.
